sections.title: Cones, Cylinders, Spheres and Pyramids

learn.title: Cubes (Let's Recall)
learn.html: A cube has 6 square faces. All the faces are the same size.

learn.title: Objects that are cubes
learn.html:
A dice 🎲 and a square wooden crate are cubes.

Every face is a square of the same size.

fig.alt: a dice and a wooden crate
fig.label: a dice and a wooden crate

learn.title: Cuboids (Let's Recall)
learn.html:
A cuboid can have 6 rectangular faces.

It can also have 4 rectangular faces and 2 square faces.

learn.title: Objects that are cuboids
learn.html:
A sponge and a juice carton are cuboids.

Their faces are rectangles.

fig.alt: a sponge and a juice carton
fig.label: a sponge and a juice carton

learn.title: Cone
learn.html:
A solid cone has 1 flat face (a circle) and 1 curved face.

It has 1 vertex (the point).

learn.title: Objects that are cones
learn.html: An ice cream cone 🍦 and a party hat 🎉 are cones.

fig.alt: an ice cream cone and a party hat
fig.label: an ice cream cone and a party hat

learn.title: Cylinder
learn.html: A solid cylinder has 2 flat faces (circles) and 1 curved face.

learn.title: Objects that are cylinders
learn.html: A can of drink 🥫, a chalk pastel and an oil drum are cylinders.

fig.alt: a can, a chalk pastel and an oil drum
fig.label: a can, a chalk pastel and an oil drum

learn.title: Sphere
learn.html:
A sphere is perfectly round. It has no flat face.

Every point on it is the same distance (the radius) from the center. Half a sphere is a hemisphere.

learn.title: Objects that are spheres
learn.html: A basketball 🏀 and a soccer ball ⚽ are spheres.

fig.alt: a basketball and a soccer ball
fig.label: a basketball and a soccer ball

learn.title: Pyramid
learn.html:
A pyramid has a flat base. Its other faces are triangles that meet at one point, the vertex.

The base can be any shape with straight edges: a triangle, a square, a trapezium, a hexagon…

learn.title: Naming pyramids
learn.html:
The base gives the name.

Square base → square pyramid (4 triangle faces).
Triangle base → triangular pyramid (3 other triangle faces).

learn.title: Prism
learn.html:
A prism has 2 faces of the same shape and size at opposite ends.

The other faces are rectangles.

learn.title: A triangular prism
learn.html:
The 2 end faces are triangles. The 3 other faces are rectangles.

A Toblerone box is a triangular prism.

learn.title: What is a net?
learn.html:
Cut along some edges of a box and open it out flat. The flat shape is a net.

A net of a solid is a flat figure that can be folded to make the solid.

learn.title: A net of a cube
learn.html:
This cross shape has 6 squares. Fold up the sides and it makes a cube.

Each square becomes one face of the cube.

learn.title: A cube has more than one net
learn.html:
There are 11 different nets of a cube. They all have 6 squares joined edge to edge.

But not every shape of 6 squares works! Two squares must never land on the same face.

learn.title: Is it a cube net? Try it!
learn.html:
Imagine folding. Pick one square as the bottom. Fold the squares around it up.

If 2 squares want to be the same face, it is not a net of a cube. A row of 4 squares with 2 squares on the same side never works.

learn.title: Nets of cuboids
learn.html:
A cuboid net has 6 rectangles: 3 pairs of the same size.

A cuboid also has more than one net.

learn.title: Check the pairs
learn.html:
This net has: 2 long wide rectangles (top and bottom), 2 long thin ones (front and back), 2 small ones (the ends).

3 matching pairs ✓. It folds into a cuboid.

learn.title: Nets of prisms
learn.html:
A triangular prism net has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles.

The triangles go on opposite sides so they become the 2 ends.

learn.title: A net of a triangular prism
learn.html:
3 rectangles in a strip, with 1 triangle on the left and 1 triangle on the right.

Fold the strip into a tube and close the ends.

learn.title: Nets of pyramids
learn.html:
A pyramid net has the base in the middle with a triangle on each edge.

Fold the triangles up and they meet at the vertex.

learn.title: A hexagonal pyramid
learn.html:
The base is a hexagon (6 sides), so there are 6 triangles.

This net makes a hexagonal pyramid.

learn.title: Nets of cylinders and cones
learn.html:
Cylinder: a rectangle (the curved face rolled flat) and 2 circles.

Cone: a fan shape (the curved face) and 1 circle.

learn.title: A net of a cone
learn.html: Roll the fan shape into a party hat. Put the circle on the bottom. It is a cone!

questions.label: Do and Learn 1
questions.q: Which of the following are the nets of a cuboid?
questions.hint: The cuboid needs 6 faces in 3 matching pairs: 2 big tops, 2 long sides, 2 small ends.
steps: The cuboid needs: 2 big rectangles, 2 long thin rectangles and 2 small end rectangles. That is 6 faces.
E: 6 faces, 3 matching pairs, and the ends are on opposite sides ✓
F: only 5 faces. One end is missing ✗
G: 7 faces. There is an extra face ✗
H: the 2 end faces are too big. They do not fit the ends of the cuboid ✗
questions.why: Only E has exactly the 6 faces of the cuboid, in the right places.

questions.label: Do and Learn 2
questions.q: Which of the following are the nets of a prism?
questions.hint: A triangular prism needs 3 rectangles and 2 triangles. The triangles must end up at opposite ends.
steps: The prism needs 3 rectangles and 2 triangles, one triangle at each end.
P: 3 rectangles, 1 triangle on the left and 1 on the right ✓
Q: 3 rectangles, triangles on opposite sides ✓
R: both triangles are on the same side. When you fold it, they cover the same end ✗
S: only 2 rectangles. The tube cannot close ✗
questions.why: P and Q have 3 rectangles and a triangle at each end.

questions.label: Do and Learn 3 (a)
questions.q: Fill in the type of solid based on the given net.
questions.hint: Look at the shapes in the net: circles, triangles, rectangles or a fan?
steps: The net has a flat base with triangles joined to it.
When you fold up the triangles, they meet at one point.
So it makes a pyramid.
questions.why: The faces in the net are the faces of the solid.

questions.label: Do and Learn 3 (b)
questions.q: Fill in the type of solid based on the given net.
questions.hint: Look at the shapes in the net: circles, triangles, rectangles or a fan?
steps: The net has a fan shape and a circle.
The fan rolls into a curved face and the circle is the base.
So it makes a cone.
questions.why: The faces in the net are the faces of the solid.

questions.label: Do and Learn 3 (c)
questions.q: Fill in the type of solid based on the given net.
questions.hint: Look at the shapes in the net: circles, triangles, rectangles or a fan?
steps: The net has a rectangle and 2 circles.
The rectangle rolls into a tube. The circles close the top and bottom.
So it makes a cylinder.
questions.why: The faces in the net are the faces of the solid.

questions.label: Do and Learn 3 (d)
questions.q: Fill in the type of solid based on the given net.
questions.hint: Look at the shapes in the net: circles, triangles, rectangles or a fan?
steps: The net has 3 rectangles and 2 triangles.
The rectangles make the sides and the triangles make the 2 ends.
So it makes a prism.
questions.why: The faces in the net are the faces of the solid.

questions.label: Exercise 1 (a)
questions.q:
Tick (✓) all the nets that form the given solid.
(a) Cube
questions.hint: Imagine folding each net. If 2 squares land on the same face, it is not a cube net.
steps: Each net has 6 squares. Now check how they fold.
Nets 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6: fold them in your mind. Every square becomes a different face ✓
Net 3: a row of 4 squares with 2 squares under the same side. The 2 squares underneath fold onto the same face, and one face stays open ✗
So tick nets 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6.
questions.why: Net 3 has two squares that fold onto the same face, so the cube cannot close.

questions.label: Exercise 1 (b)
questions.q:
Tick (✓) all the nets that form the given solid.
(b) Pyramid (a triangular pyramid)
questions.hint: This pyramid has 4 faces, and all 4 are triangles.
steps: The triangular pyramid has a triangle base and 3 triangle sides: 4 triangles.
Net 1: a strip of 4 triangles ✓
Net 2: a big triangle made of 4 triangles ✓
Net 3: it has a square base. That makes a square pyramid, not this one ✗
Net 4: it has 5 triangles. That is one too many ✗
questions.why: Only nets 1 and 2 have exactly 4 triangles.

questions.label: Exercise 1 (c)
questions.q:

(c) Cuboid
questions.hint: Look at the faces in the net: 2 small squares and 4 long rectangles.
steps: The net has 2 small squares (the ends) and 4 long thin rectangles (the sides).
So the cuboid must be long and thin with square ends.
1 is a small cube (6 squares) ✗. 2 is wide and flat ✗. 4 is tall but its ends are not squares ✗.

questions.why: Its faces match the net: 2 squares and 4 long rectangles.

questions.label: Exercise 2
questions.q: Janice wants to make a prism from a net. What are the possible positions, a, b or c, that she should place the rectangular face to complete the net of the prism?
questions.hint: The net needs 3 rectangles in a ring. The new rectangle must join on to make the third side of the tube.
steps: The net has 2 rectangles and 2 triangles. A triangular prism needs 3 rectangles.
c: below the bottom rectangle. The 3 rectangles make a strip that folds into a tube ✓
a: joined to the slanted side of the left triangle. It folds round to become the third side ✓
b: next to the top rectangle on the right. It would stick out past the end and cover the triangle's place ✗
questions.why: Positions a and c both make the 3 rectangles join edge to edge around the triangles.

questions.label: Exercise 3 (a)

questions.hint: A column of 4 squares makes the 4 sides around the cube. You need a top and a bottom.
steps: The 4 blue squares in a column fold round into a ring: front, top, back, bottom.
You still need the 2 side faces: one square on the left of the column and one on the right.
They can be next to any of the 4 blue squares, one on each side.
The pink squares show the answer in the key. Fold it in your mind: all 6 faces are different ✓
questions.answer: See the pink squares in the picture
questions.why: One square on each side of the column of 4 always makes a cube net.

learn.title: Unit 8 big ideas
learn.html:
Cone: 1 circle + 1 curved face. Cylinder: 2 circles + 1 curved face. Sphere: no flat face.

Pyramid: base + triangles meeting at a vertex. Prism: same shape at both ends.

learn.title: Faces, vertices and edges
learn.html:
Face: a flat surface. Edge: where 2 faces meet. Vertex: a corner point.

For these solids: F + V - E = 2.

learn.title: Volume of a cuboid (from Unit 12 ideas)
learn.html:
Volume = Length × Width × Height.

A 2 cm by 3 cm by 4 cm box: 2 × 3 × 4 = 24 cm³.

questions.label: Let's Think Along
questions.q: Find the number of faces (F), vertices (V) and edges (E) of a cube, a cuboid, a prism and a pyramid. Then find F + V - E for each one. What do you notice?
questions.hint: Count carefully. Mark each face, vertex or edge as you count it.
steps: Triangular prism: F = 5 (2 triangles + 3 rectangles), V = 6, E = 9. 5 + 6 - 9 = 2
Square pyramid: F = 5 (1 square + 4 triangles), V = 5, E = 8. 5 + 5 - 8 = 2
Every answer is 2!
questions.answer: F + V - E = 2 for all of them
questions.why: For these solids, faces + vertices - edges always equals 2.

questions.label: Problem Solving
questions.q: The figure shows a net of a cuboid. Find the volume of the cuboid.
questions.hint: The 26 cm is made of 4 sides: 10 cm, the short side, 10 cm, the short side.
steps: Understand: The net is a cuboid. We know 10 cm, 12 cm and 26 cm. We must find the volume.
Along the 26 cm there are 4 faces: 10 cm + short + 10 cm + short.
Short side + short side = 26 - 10 - 10 = 6 cm
Short side = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm
Volume of cuboid = Length × Width × Height = 12 × 10 × 3
Check: work backward. 360 ÷ 3 = 120 and 120 ÷ 10 = 12 ✓
questions.why: The cuboid is 12 cm by 10 cm by 3 cm, and 12 × 10 × 3 = 360.

questions.label: Math Journal
questions.q: If Su Ling were to cut a pyramid into 2 pieces as shown below, would she get a pyramid and a prism? Give your reasons.
questions.hint: A prism has 2 end faces that are the same shape AND size. Look at the bottom piece.
steps: The top piece has a flat base and triangle faces that meet at a vertex. It is a pyramid.
The bottom piece has a small square on top and a big square at the bottom. They are not the same size.
Its side faces are not rectangles or parallelograms (they are trapeziums).
So the bottom piece is not a prism.
questions.answer: She would get a pyramid, but not a prism.
questions.why: A prism needs identical faces at opposite ends and rectangle (or parallelogram) sides. The bottom piece has neither.
